findings.title: Rendering a DOCX can bypass XML depth limits through auxiliary part names
findings.summary: A crafted DOCX can name a styles, header, footer, or note XML part with a non-.xml/.rels extension. Admission skips its XML policy, but relationship-based rendering parses it recursively. Deep nesting can exhaust the process stack and terminate native consumers or trap WASM execution.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger process availability loss through ordinary rendering APIs without host privileges. Impact is availability of the processing worker, not code execution or data disclosure; deployment-level blast radius is unknown.
severity.changeConditions: Dedicated resource-limited subprocesses reduce impact; a long-lived shared rendering process increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent static trace establishes extension-gated validation, relationship-selected unchecked sinks, and recursion without a depth check. No runtime crash reproduction was executed.

taxonomy.category: XML resource limit bypass / uncontrolled recursion

codeEvidence.label: Admission scans XML by filename suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker chooses the entry name; auxiliary .bin payloads take the non-XML drain branch and never receive check_xml_depth or its shared tag policy.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering performs the incomplete admission first
codeEvidence.explanation: Untrusted document bytes reach the renderer and pass admission and bounded package loading; neither normalization nor package loading adds a policy check on non-XML-named auxiliary content.

codeEvidence.label: Relationships select arbitrary auxiliary part names
codeEvidence.explanation: A valid internal styles relationship can select styles.bin; the selection does not require the .xml extension used by the admission gate.

codeEvidence.label: Styles bytes reach unchecked DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The styles string loaded at line 3480 from main_rel_part is forwarded to the permissive parser. With link styles disabled the malicious nesting is unchanged.

codeEvidence.label: DOM parser recurses on each nested element
codeEvidence.explanation: Every attacker-controlled nested opening tag adds a Rust stack frame. This raw parser has no depth limit; skipped admission therefore allows stack exhaustion with a relatively small part.

rootCause.summary: The document supplier controls both auxiliary ZIP names and relationship targets. `admit()` applies `check_xml_depth()` only to .xml/.rels entries and separately the main document part. Rendering selects styles by relationship type via `main_rel_part()`, loads that nonstandard filename, and calls unchecked `parse_xdocument()`. That parser recurses for each nested element, so the filename decision removes the depth guard from the actual parser input. Headers/footers and endnotes use the same unsafe assumption.

findings.remediation: Validate every part that will be interpreted as XML under the active InputLimits regardless of filename. Use checked parsing at auxiliary consumers or identify all XML content types/relationship-selected parts during admission, preserving typed refusal behavior before DOM construction.

counterEvidence: Compressed, inflated-byte and entry-count limits still apply.
The main part is explicitly checked even with an unusual extension.
Markdown Package::xml has its own checked parsing; this finding establishes the conversion path.
SECURITY.md recommends CPU/memory-limited processing; that mitigates blast radius but does not enforce the promised XML depth gate.
limitations: No application execution, crash probe, tests or live deployment inspection.
validation.summary: Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.

dataflow.summary: DOCX ZIP entry + internal relationship -> extension-based admission skip -> PartFs -> main_rel_part -> load_stylesheet -> parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.

impact.why: Stack exhaustion can terminate a native processing worker or trap a WASM call.

likelihood.why: Relationship targets and nested XML are attacker-controlled and require no optional privileged configuration.

reachability.summary: Public byte-based conversion APIs accept caller-provided DOCX. An attacker needs only to supply a document that another user or service renders; no remote service deployment is assumed.
preconditions: Auxiliary relationship selects a non-.xml/.rels payload with nesting beyond the configured depth

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with a normal main document and an internal styles relationship pointing to a non-.xml/.rels part containing excessive nested XML, then request PDF/PNG rendering.

remediationTests: Render a package with a styles relationship to deeply nested styles.bin and assert INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Cover header/footer, notes, diagram and text-box relationship targets with nonstandard extensions and active depth/tag budgets.
Verify valid nonstandard auxiliary filenames continue to render.

originalCandidates.originalEvidence: src/admission.rs:537-566 only scans .xml/.rels and 578-591 rechecks main part only. A header/footer/styles/notes relationship may target .bin yet convert/mod.rs uses parse_xdocument unchecked. XML permissive parser recursively parse_element (exact sink lines still under investigation). Markdown Package::xml separately parse_xml_with_limits so likely protected.

findings.title: Converting Markdown can exhaust the stack on cyclic drawing dependencies
findings.summary: An untrusted Markdown drawing payload can encode a dependency cycle. Markdown-to-DOCX assembly recursively materializes the graph without a visited set or depth/work budget, causing nontermination and stack exhaustion from a small input.

severity.rationale: Ordinary untrusted Markdown conversion can terminate a native processing worker or trap WASM. Availability impact is bounded to the process or call; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Resource-limited subprocess isolation reduces service impact; shared long-lived conversion workers increase it.

confidence.rationale: Static trace confirms direct public Markdown input, unconstrained graph deserialization and unconditional recursive revisiting. No runtime reproduction was run.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion in drawing dependency graph

codeEvidence.label: Markdown image destinations decode caller payloads
codeEvidence.explanation: Markdown suppliers can provide a drawing destination directly; success stores the decoded graph for package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded JSON becomes a dependency graph without validation
codeEvidence.explanation: Serde validates JSON shape but not graph acyclicity. Flat vectors of relationships with in-range indices satisfy deserialization even when cyclic.

codeEvidence.label: Materialization begins recursive dependency expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: An internal top-level relationship selects a caller-controlled dependency index and starts dep_part; the only graph check is that the index fits.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency expansion revisits cyclic indices
codeEvidence.explanation: used records output filenames, not dependency indices. An in-range self-edge recursively expands the same dependency before any package caching or termination step can occur.

rootCause.summary: `markdown_to_docx()` reads image destinations and accepts a caller-supplied `drawing:` envelope. `decode()` deserializes its flat dependency vector and `part` indices without graph validation. Package assembly invokes `materialize()`, which follows a top-level index into `dep_part()`. Each nested in-range index recursively invokes `dep_part()` again. The `used` set tracks renamed package files, so it neither detects an active index nor memoizes completed graph nodes; a self-edge never reaches the later byte comparison or package write.

findings.remediation: Validate dependency graphs and budgets at drawing decode/materialization. Reject active-node revisits with a typed conversion error, memoize completed dependency indices, and enforce total dependency, edge, byte and traversal budgets before output assembly.

counterEvidence: MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS bound capture from DOCX, but are not applied by decode and do not prevent even a single-node cycle.
The package byte-equality reuse check at drawing.rs:1998 runs after recursive children and is unreachable for cycles.
limitations: No application execution, crash probe or tests.
validation.summary: Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.

dataflow.summary: Markdown image destination -> decode(base64 JSON) -> Document.drawings -> Relate::drawing -> materialize -> dep_part -> repeated dependency index.

impact.why: Unbounded stack consumption can abort native processing or trap WASM execution.

likelihood.why: The input is accepted by the normal conversion path and a flat JSON graph can express a cycle without violating deserializer nesting bounds.

reachability.summary: Public Rust Markdown conversion accepts strings directly; Python and WASM wrappers call the same conversion. No reference document, external image loader, network or privileged options are required.

attackPath.summary: Supply Markdown containing a drawing envelope whose top-level internal dependency leads to a cycle, then invoke Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.

remediationTests: Assert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle return a typed refusal without stack overflow.
Assert a shared acyclic dependency materializes once and preserves relationships.
Apply decode-side dependency/edge/byte budgets to external Markdown envelopes.

originalCandidates.originalEvidence: src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs::decode (1397-1408) accepts arbitrary base64 JSON Drawing with caller-controlled deps/rel.part; materialize (1892-1894) calls dep_part; dep_part (1971-1973) recursively follows inner indexes without cycle detection/depth/work budget. A one-dep payload whose dep.rels[0].part=0 causes unbounded recursion/stack overflow during markdown_to_docx, reachable Rust/Python/WASM/Node convert. MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS only constrain DOCX capture, not decode. Checking package caller and other guards now; likely CWE-674 medium availability finding.
